sections.title: Document
sections.summary: # Microarchitecture https://huggingface.co/datasets/s-nlp/kilt Wikipedia ID: 1410175 In computer engineering, microarchitecture, also called computer organization and sometimes abbreviated as "µarch"

sections.title: Microarchitecture
sections.summary: Introduction defining microarchitecture as the implementation of an ISA in a specific processor.

sections.title: Relation to instruction set architecture.
sections.summary: Explains how microarchitecture implements the programming model defined by the ISA.

sections.title: Aspects of microarchitecture.
sections.summary: Discusses core components like pipelined datapaths, execution units, and system-level design constraints.

sections.title: Microarchitectural concepts.
sections.summary: Overview section for various techniques used to improve processor performance and efficiency.

sections.title: See also.
sections.summary: List of related topics including CPU architectures, hardware description languages, and computing models.

sections.title: Instruction cycles.
sections.summary: Describes the fundamental steps of reading, decoding, processing, and writing instructions.

sections.title: Multicycle Microarchitecture.
sections.summary: Details designs that execute instructions over multiple clock cycles, often using microprogramming.

sections.title: Increasing execution speed.
sections.summary: Addresses memory hierarchy delays and the evolution toward parallel instruction execution.

sections.title: Instruction set choice.
sections.summary: Analyzes the impact of CISC vs. RISC and other ISA choices on hardware complexity and performance.

sections.title: Instruction pipelining.
sections.summary: Explains how overlapping instruction stages increases throughput, particularly in RISC designs.

sections.title: Cache.
sections.summary: Describes on-die cache memory hierarchies and their synergy with pipelining to reduce stalls.

sections.title: Branch prediction.
sections.summary: Covers techniques for predicting conditional branches to minimize pipeline flushes and speculative execution.

sections.title: Superscalar.
sections.summary: Introduces processors capable of executing multiple instructions simultaneously via replicated functional units.

sections.title: Out-of-order execution.
sections.summary: Explains reordering instructions to avoid data dependency stalls while maintaining program order results.

sections.title: Register renaming.
sections.summary: Technique to eliminate false dependencies between instructions by mapping logical registers to physical ones.

sections.title: Multiprocessing and multithreading.
sections.summary: Discusses multi-core systems and simultaneous multithreading to exploit higher levels of parallelism.
